questions.q: According to this lesson, how are models organized across folders in a real dbt project?
options: Randomly, since dbt ignores folder structure entirely
By which developer wrote the file
By what stage of transformation they represent (e.g. staging vs. marts), not just by file type
Alphabetically, with no other logic
questions.explain: Folders mirror the data's transformation stage — staging models live in staging/, business-facing models live in marts/.

questions.q: What lives in a project's `marts/` folder?
options: Nothing — marts is reserved exclusively for tests
Only raw source declarations
Database credentials
The final, business-facing models that analysts and BI tools actually query
questions.explain: marts/ holds the final, business-facing models — the output layer analysts and BI tools query.

questions.q: What third layer does this lesson say most real dbt projects converge on, between staging and marts?
options: A second copy of the raw sources
Intermediate — joins and logic that aren't yet a final model, kept separate to keep marts models readable
A layer exclusively for storing test results
A caching layer that duplicates every staging model
questions.explain: Intermediate models hold joins/logic that aren't final business-facing models, existing to keep marts models clean and readable — covered fully in Chapter 3.

questions.q: Does moving a model's .sql file to a different folder change how dbt resolves its ref() calls?
options: Yes — ref() calls break immediately if a file moves folders
It depends on which warehouse is being used
No — folder location is organizational only; ref() resolves by model name, not file path
Yes — moving a file to marts/ automatically changes its materialization
questions.explain: ref() resolves by model name, not by folder path, so reorganizing folders is purely organizational and doesn't affect how dbt builds anything.

questions.q: What is the one organizing principle this lesson says keeps a project navigable at any size?
options: Every model must live in exactly one giant folder
Folders mirror the data's transformation stage, not just its business subject
Folder names must match the warehouse's schema names exactly
Only one model is allowed per folder
questions.explain: Keeping folders aligned to transformation stage (staging vs. marts, etc.) is what makes a project's contents predictable at a glance, at any scale.
